steps.title: Prepare stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 10× Yamamoto’s Ringer’s solution by dissolving 75 g NaCl, 2.0 g KCl, 2.7 g CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 2 g NaHCO₃ in water and bring the volume to 1 L; autoclave, then add 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin solution per 500 mL. Make 100× hatching buffer by dissolving 100 g NaCl, 3 g KCl, 4 g CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 16 g MgSO₄·7H₂O in water to 1 L. Store the 10× Ringer’s at 4 °C, the hatching buffer at room temperature, and keep hatching enzyme at –80 °C.

steps.title: Linearize plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: For each plasmid (pMTB‑AC‑TagGFP2 or pMTB‑α‑bungarotoxin) set up a 20 µL restriction digest with 2 µg plasmid, 2 µL 10× CutSmart buffer, 1 µL EcoRV (for AC‑TagGFP2) or AvaI (for α‑bungarotoxin), and water to volume; incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Verify and purify linear DNA
steps.instruction: Run 1 µL of each digest on an agarose gel to confirm complete linearization. Purify the full reaction with the Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean‑up kit, eluting DNA in 25 µL water. Measure concentration with a NanoDrop; it should be ~100 ng/µL.

steps.title: In‑vitro transcription of mRNA
steps.instruction: Thaw the mMESSAGE mMACHINE SP6 kit (except the enzyme mix) at room temperature. In a tube combine nuclease‑free water to a total volume of 10 µL, 5 µL 2× NTP/CAP, 2 µL 10× reaction buffer, 2 µL linear DNA template (0.5–1 µg), and 1 µL enzyme mix; mix gently and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Digest DNA template and purify mRNA
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL TURBO DNase to the transcription reaction and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min. Purify the mRNA with the RNeasy Mini kit, eluting in 30 µL nuclease‑free water. Measure concentration (100–500 ng/µL) and A260/280 (~2.0) on a NanoDrop; optionally verify integrity on an agarose gel. Store purified mRNA at –80 °C (stable for months).

steps.title: Prepare injection agarose gel
steps.instruction: Melt 1 % agarose in hatching buffer, keep 20 mL molten. Pour into a 9 cm plastic dish, slide the injection mold onto the surface at a 45° angle to avoid air bubbles, and let solidify. Once solid, remove the mold and overlay the gel with hatching buffer to prevent drying. Store the gel at 4 °C for up to several months.

steps.title: Pull and store injection needles
steps.instruction: Use a Narishige capillary puller with heater setting 57.5 and mode selector set to step 1 to pull glass capillaries into microinjection needles. Store the needles in a protective container so the fragile tips do not touch anything.

steps.title: Set up breeding and collect eggs
steps.instruction: The evening before injection, place adult medaka pairs in a tank separated by a transparent partition. In the morning, remove the partition; mating occurs within 5–10 min. After fertilization, collect eggs with a fine‑mesh fish‑scooping net, remove chorion filaments, and transfer eggs into hatching buffer.

steps.title: Prepare injection solution
steps.instruction: Mix the following to a final volume of 10 µL: Actin‑Chromobody‑TagGFP2 mRNA (amount not specified), 1.5 µg α‑bungarotoxin mRNA, 0.25 µg 0.5 % phenol red, and nuclease‑free water to reach 10 µL.

steps.title: Load needle and set pressures
steps.instruction: Load ~3 µL of the injection solution into a glass needle using a Microloader tip. Attach the needle to the injector, set injection pressure (Pi) to ~500 hPa and compensation pressure (Pc) to ~150 hPa. Gently scratch the chorion surface with the needle tip to break it until solution slowly leaks from the tip.

steps.title: Inject embryos at 4‑cell stage
steps.instruction: Place the embryos on the injection gel (covered with hatching buffer) and align them in the wells with forceps. When embryos reach the 4‑cell stage, inject ~2–3 nL (≈½ cell volume) of the solution into the cytoplasm of one cell per embryo to achieve mosaic expression.

steps.title: Incubate injected embryos
steps.instruction: Keep the injected embryos in hatching buffer at 23–32 °C. Dechorionation will be performed later on the same day.

steps.title: Dechorionate embryos with hatching enzyme
steps.instruction: Dilute hatching enzyme 1:5–1:20 in ½× Yamamoto’s Ringer’s solution (start with 1:20 for a new lot). Transfer embryos to a small‑bottom container (e.g., 4‑well dish), remove excess medium, add the diluted enzyme, and incubate at 28 °C. Monitor every 30–60 min; digestion usually completes in 2–3 h, leaving a thin membranous layer. If digestion is incomplete, increase enzyme concentration.

steps.title: Rinse and transfer embryos
steps.instruction: After chorion digestion, gently rinse embryos in a glass dish filled with Yamamoto’s Ringer’s solution to remove enzyme. Transfer embryos to a fresh glass dish with Ringer’s solution (glass preferred to avoid damage from plastic surfaces).

steps.title: Incubate to desired stage
steps.instruction: Maintain embryos in Yamamoto’s Ringer’s at 23–32 °C until they reach the target developmental stage (stage 28 requires ~3 days at 26 °C).

steps.title: Mount embryos in low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 % low‑melting‑point agarose in hot Yamamoto’s Ringer’s and keep at ~40 °C. Place a few drops of the agarose on the glass‑bottom of a glass‑bottom dish, immediately transfer 2–3 screened embryos (GFP‑positive) into the drops, and orient them so the region of interest contacts the glass. Allow the agarose to solidify within ~1 min. If orientation is wrong, add Ringer’s, break the agarose with forceps, and repeat.

steps.title: Image embryos with confocal microscope
steps.instruction: Start the inverted confocal microscope and Zen software. Use a 25× water‑immersion objective, locate the ROI by visual inspection through the eyepieces, and screen for GFP fluorescence. Switch to the 40× water‑immersion objective for subcellular resolution and acquire images. For timelapse, enable the Time‑Series option; if imaging for hours, install a heating chamber to keep the sample at the appropriate temperature.
